AC3: 'returns a certified PASS with zero blocking findings'
The P4 cap 'refuses a plan review outright' — so the epic's content has never passed a full review; admission only removes the P4 finding, not any content findings that may then appear
findings.finding: The approach only shortens the description to clear the P4 admission cap, but AC3 requires a certified PASS with ZERO blocking findings. Because the 10,135-char epic was never content-reviewed (P4 blocked at admission), admitting it may surface previously-hidden content findings that trimming length alone does not resolve, leaving a gap between the planned step and the stated end-state.

findings.checklist_item: State a positive rationale for editing the epic description rather than relaxing/exempting the retroactive admission cap (verify.max_ticket_description_chars), and verify the claim that shortening the parent would invalidate sibling children's plan-review attestations (a child's material fingerprint appears to cover only its own description).
evidence: Context: 'The epic's description predates the cap; it is not defective, merely over a limit introduced after it was authored.'
Approach: 'The epic's owner shortens the description to at most 8,000 characters ... then runs rebar review-plan'

verify.max_ticket_description_chars is a real config key (det_floor._description_limit -> config.load_config(repo_root).verify.max_ticket_description_chars), so relaxing/exempting is a genuine alternative the plan does not weigh

The plan's supporting rationale that editing 'would invalidate any plan-review attestation already held by its other children' is doubtful: a child's attestation manifest fingerprints its OWN description (bloated-shadeful-lamprey's signature lists 'material-part: description ... 7978' for the child), not the parent's, so parent-description edits may not invalidate sibling attestations.
findings.finding: The plan chooses to edit the ticket's description but gives no positive rationale for that mechanism over the structurally-different alternative of adjusting the retroactively-introduced admission cap (verify.max_ticket_description_chars), even though the plan's own Context argues the description 'is not defective, merely over a limit introduced after it was authored' — the exact framing that makes a policy-layer fix plausible.
scenarios: A reviewer or the epic owner asks why a non-defective, retroactively-over-cap description must be rewritten rather than the cap adjusted or the pre-cap ticket exempted.
The condensation invalidates the epic's OWN future attestation basis while the stated sibling-invalidation justification turns out not to apply.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one or two sentences to Approach justifying content-editing over a config change (e.g. the cap is a deliberate resource-protection invariant that should hold for all tickets including pre-cap ones, so exempting is undesirable), and either substantiate or drop the sibling-attestation-invalidation rationale after confirming what each child's material fingerprint actually covers.

findings.finding: The mechanism from AC2 (review-plan admits the plan) to AC3 (claim exits 0) is incomplete: clearing the P4 admission cap only lets the review RUN; it does not guarantee a PASS verdict nor a persisted/signed attestation, both of which the parent-first cascade requires before a child can be claimed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an intermediate criterion: `rebar review-plan 0e68-41eb-5782-4336` returns a certified PASS with zero blocking findings and a persisted plan-review attestation on the epic, before AC3's claim check.
